summary: No adverse issuer, custodian, administrator, depositary or swap-counterparty event was found this week for Vanguard, iShares/BlackRock, Invesco, Xtrackers (DWS) or SPDR (State Street), or for the custodians and swap banks behind the owner's world, S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 lines. The only issuer change found is DWS's switch to the global umbrella brand Deutsche Asset Management. It was announced on 2026-09-08 and rolls out from early November 2026. DWS says Xtrackers fund names, products, contracts and service providers stay the same, so it is recorded as information for XSPU.L and XNAS.L. The explorer findings cover AI-sector credit stress: CoreWeave bonds at about 15-16%, SoftBank CDS near 500bp, Oracle near junk and a chipmaker CDS basket at about 160bp. None of these names is an ETF issuer, depositary or swap counterparty, and this week's searches found no confirmed spread stress at the bank swap counterparties (Goldman, JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, Deutsche Bank). No Central Bank of Ireland, CSSF or FCA sanction against an issuer or depositary was found. Coverage limit: there was no direct scan of the regulators' enforcement pages or of each fund's RNS feed, so the result is 'nothing adverse found', not 'confirmed clear'.

events.issue: Issuer rebrand: DWS adopts Deutsche Asset Management as its global umbrella brand, rolling out from early November 2026 and due to finish by March 2027. Xtrackers keeps its name, and DWS says products, contracts and services are unchanged. No change to the management company, depositary, swap counterparties or ISIN was announced.
